What is the equation of the ellipse given above?
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(4,-2),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=1,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=3.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-4)^{2}}{{1}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-2))^{2}}{{3}^{2}} & =1 \\ (x-4)^{2}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{9} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
